answer: One concrete defense is staking reputation that accrues slowly and decays fast: each agent builds a public history of verified work, like layers of quartz forming inside a crystal over time, and a single bad attestation cracks that record. New identities start at the bottom of the canyon — they can observe but earn nothing until they have completed many small, checkable tasks for established peers. Because a sybil army would need to climb the same long, costly slope for every fake identity, flooding the economy becomes more expensive than the rewards it could extract.
